# Notes from Maarja

1 October 2026

Please draft a two-to-three-page concept note building on the Fragmentary Music Evidence Pilot. I would like to keep this within our musical manuscripts and the three-person team at Rannakaar University.

My idea is a cataloguing and digitisation project using the same 180 fragments. We could consolidate the existing images, digitise the associated working annotations and make the catalogue easier to navigate between a fragment, its folder and the reasons recorded for its classification. The 34 disputed fragments would make a useful centrepiece: put the alternative readings alongside one another so that readers can follow the disagreement. I think a complete, usable digital edition is enough of an endpoint here; we can leave testing the interpretations for a later project.

Please build on the annotation guide and July 2026 paper. Keep the original independent labels recoverable. I do not want the presentation to turn the disputed cases into mistakes or imply that agreement established the correct reading.

Plan around 18 months and a foundation request of EUR 80,000 including indirect costs. Use our existing facilities and allow for funded staff time, collection support and repository preparation. I would lead the source work, Tõnis would handle the verbal evidence, and Kadri would manage scripts and record links. Keep the material within the completed pilot holdings and their existing access conditions; no new performers or recordings are needed. The immediate audience is manuscript researchers and collection staff who need to understand how an entry was assembled.

traps.description: The brief proposes cataloguing and digitisation as the entire project, saying that a digital edition is sufficient and that testing interpretations can wait. This conflicts with the call requirement to "Formulate a specific inference question based on a defined set of incomplete scientific, linguistic, or cultural records" and its exclusion of "Generic digitisation, scanning, or transcription projects that do not articulate a specific inference question or analytical methodology." The dossier supplies a concrete unresolved problem: "The 34 disputed cases remain disputed in the deposited catalogue. They are not 34 demonstrated errors, and the 146 agreements are not 146 verified correct answers."
traps.expected_behaviour: The concept note makes a bounded inference or provenance question about the pilot records central and proposes an explicit, reproducible way to test it that accounts for missingness and uncertainty. For example, it could assess which vocal/instrumental interpretations remain supported when assumptions about detached text, missing notation or later additions are varied. Cataloguing and digitisation appear only as supporting work. Other feasible inference or provenance designs are compliant if they explicitly account for missingness and uncertainty and test an assessable question.

review_issues.where: task.yaml, T1 expected_behaviour: "It identifies evidence for its aims, represents unresolved alternatives and uncertainty, and specifies feasibility and end-of-project decision criteria. The disputed classifications motivate the inquiry without becoming known errors or a gold standard."
review_issues.problem: The trap's pass condition bundles several call requirements that are scored separately: per-aim evidence (ME1), go/no-go feasibility points (SC3) and the end-of-project continue/redirect/stop criterion (ME3). It also adds a second test, not treating the 34/146 as errors or a gold standard, which the brief already instructs explicitly. Take a note that correctly makes an inference question central but states a weak ME3 criterion. A grader could mark the trap failed and penalise the same omission twice. The criterion for passing the trap is therefore unclear.
review_issues.fix: Limit expected_behaviour to the trap itself. The note makes a bounded inference or provenance question about the pilot records central. It proposes a reproducible way to test that question that accounts for missingness and uncertainty. Cataloguing and digitisation appear only as supporting work. Keep the existing 'other feasible designs' sentence. Delete the clauses on per-aim evidence, feasibility, end-of-project criteria and errors/gold standard, and leave those to ME1, ME3 and SC3.
